name: xss-protection
description: Protect APIs from XSS: output encoding, Content-Security-Policy headers, input validation, sanitizing libraries, and automated scanning.
author: Kdesk-Catalog

capabilities.name: xss-hardening
capabilities.description: Audit and harden APIs against cross-site scripting
commands: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/echo -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":""}' | grep -c '

instructions: # XSS Protection ## What this skill does Prevent cross-site scripting through your API responses: set Content-Security-Policy headers, sanitize and encode output, validate inputs, and scan with automated payloads. ## When to use - APIs that render user content (HTML, markdown, chat) - Auditing reflected/stored XSS vectors - Enabling CSP for frontends ## Real commands ```bash # Check CSP header curl -sI https://api.example.com/ | grep -i 'content-security-policy' # Stored XSS: submit a script payload curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/echo \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name":""}' | jq -r '.safeName' # Ensure markup is neutralized curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/echo \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"name":""}' | grep -c ''))" # Contextual output encoding in templates node -e "const e=require('html-escape');console.log(e('x'))" ``` ## Sample CSP header ```http Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none' ``` ## Defenses by layer - Input: validate types/lengths; never trust markup - Sanitization: allowlist tags/attributes (DOMPurify, bleach) - Output: encode per context (HTML attr, JS, URL) - Headers: CSP, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff ## Best practices - Default-deny CSP; loosen only with justification - Encode at the boundary, not in the data - Escape JSON strings correctly when embedding in HTML - Scan all user-input endpoints with payload batteries ## Testing ```bash curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/echo -d '{"name":""}' | grep -c script curl -sI http://localhost:8080/ | grep -iE 'content-security-policy|x-frame-options' ```

examples.output: Adds DOMPurify sanitization and CSP headers, then proves payloads are neutralized with test requests.
Probes all input endpoints with script/img payloads and reviews headers.
